title: Baryogenesis via the CKM Matrix with Minimal Flavor Violation
summary: It is often claimed Standard Model CP violation is insufficient for baryogenesis. We present a counterexample using minimal flavor violation (MFV) in which all CP-violating effects arise from the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) matrix. Our scenario involves a leptoquark field with MFV-preserving interactions whose decays to Standard Model particles yield the observed baryon asymmetry in the early universe. Unlike previous efforts to realize baryogenesis through the CP violation of the CKM matrix, our scenario does not require any time-variation of model parameters.

title: Axion-driven spontaneous leptogenesis, precisely
summary: We revisit a minimal scenario for spontaneous leptogenesis where the asymmetry generation is driven by a heavy axion-like field evolving via standard misalignment. We focus on the simplest framework in which lepton number violation originates from the dimension-five Weinberg operator and contributions from standard thermal leptogenesis become negligible. The asymmetry is computed by solving a set of transport equations, which incorporate fully flavor-dependent interaction rates for the Weinberg operator that are presented here for the first time. We also derive a simple algebraic master formula for the generated $B\!-\!L$ asymmetry, valid for arbitrary axion velocities and classically shift-symmetric couplings to the Standard Model, that reproduces the $B\!-\!L$-production dynamics of the full set of transport equations in controlled parameter regions. Along the way, we quantify the importance of low-scale neutrino masses and the two mass orderings on the final prediction for the generated asymmetry. Finally, we assess the cosmological viability of different axion couplings by accounting for entropy dilution from late-time axion decays and imposing constraints from baryonic isocurvature perturbations. We demonstrate that explaining the baryon asymmetry via standard Majoron misalignment is under severe tension due to dilution from late-time decays. In contrast, axions coupled to strong or weak sphalerons can successfully produce the observed asymmetry for decay constants near the energy scale of grand unification and axion oscillation temperatures $T_{\text{osc}} \gtrsim 10^{11\cdots12}$ GeV, provided a cosmological history featuring high-scale inflation and efficient reheating.

They derive a simple algebraic master formula and show that Majoron misalignment is under severe tension due to dilution, while axions coupled to sphalerons can succeed for decay constants near the GUT scale and T_osc ≳ 10^11-12 GeV under high-scale inflation.

The study aims to provide first flavor-dependent transport equations and evaluate the cosmological viability of different axion couplings.

Successful baryogenesis requires high-scale inflation and efficient reheating with large decay constants.

title: First-principles upper bounds on dark matter-electron scattering rates from condensed matter sum rules
summary: A wide variety of condensed matter systems are used or proposed as detectors to search for dark matter-electron scattering. In general, the scattering rate depends on detailed knowledge of the electronic properties of these systems. However, when dark matter couples to electron density, the dark matter-electron scattering rate can be related to the electron energy loss function, whose integrals are bounded by first-principles sum rules that rely on only a few macroscopic target properties. In this paper, we use these first-principles sum rules to derive upper bounds on the dark matter-electron scattering rate depending on only a few material properties: the plasma frequency $ω_\text{p}$, the target mass density $ρ_T$, and the static (longitudinal) dielectric function at finite momentum transfer, $\varepsilon(q, 0)$. The bulk material properties $ω_\text{p}$ and $ρ_T$ vary only over a limited range across a wide variety of materials, and to a good approximation, the generic large-$q$ dependence of $\varepsilon(q, 0)$ can be understood from a simple scaling law depending only on $ω_\text{p}$ which we verify with analytic and numerical examples. Thus, our upper bounds are largely material-agnostic, and place a fundamental limit on the sensitivity of any dark matter-electron direct detection experiment probing the coupling to electron density.

AI.tldr: This paper derives fundamental upper bounds on the dark matter-electron scattering rate using first-principles sum rules related to the electron energy loss function. These bounds depend only on a few macroscopic material properties—plasma frequency, mass density, and the static longitudinal dielectric function—making them largely material-agnostic and setting a fundamental sensitivity limit for any direct detection experiment probing dark matter coupling to electron density.
AI.motivation: Dark matter-electron scattering detection rates typically depend on detailed knowledge of electronic properties of various condensed matter detector systems. The authors seek to establish fundamental, material-independent limits on the scattering rate using first-principles sum rules, so that the maximum possible sensitivity of any experiment can be understood without requiring detailed microscopic calculations for each candidate material.
AI.method: The authors use first-principles sum rules bounding the integrals of the electron energy loss function to derive upper bounds on the dark matter-electron scattering rate. These bounds depend only on three material properties: the plasma frequency ω_p, the mass density ρ_T, and the static longitudinal dielectric function ε(q,0). They show that the finite-momentum dependence of ε(q,0) follows a simple scaling law depending only on ω_p, verified with analytic and numerical examples.
AI.result: The derived upper bounds are expressed in terms of only the plasma frequency, target mass density, and static dielectric function. Since ω_p and ρ_T vary only over a limited range across different materials, and the large-q behavior of ε(q,0) can be approximated by a simple scaling law based on ω_p alone, the bounds are largely material-agnostic and impose a fundamental limit on detector sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: The upper bounds place a fundamental limit on the sensitivity of any dark matter-electron direct detection experiment probing the coupling to electron density, independent of detailed material-specific calculations.

title: Novel Signatures of Matter-Induced Dark Matter Decay in Large-Volume Neutrino Telescopes
summary: Large-volume neutrino telescopes offer a unique opportunity to search for decaying dark matter through events containing a pair of energetic, highly non-collimated muon tracks emerging from a common vertex. Such events would have negligible Standard Model backgrounds and would constitute a striking signature of new physics. Conventional dark matter annihilation or decay, however, is too strongly constrained to produce an observable rate of such events. We therefore consider scenarios in which an excited dark matter state is extremely long-lived in vacuum but decays much more rapidly in the presence of ordinary matter. We present two realizations of this mechanism. In the first, a long-range scalar field sourced by ordinary matter modifies the dark-sector mass spectrum, kinematically opening the decay $χ_2 \rightarrow χ_1 Z'$ near the Earth while leaving it forbidden in vacuum. In the second, the scalar background induces kinetic mixing between a heavy $Z'$ and the photon, greatly enhancing the three-body decay $χ_2\toχ_1μ^+μ^-$ in matter-rich environments. We calculate the resulting distributions of muon energies and opening angles and show that viable regions of parameter space can yield observable event rates in IceCube, KM3NeT, and other large-volume neutrino telescopes while remaining consistent with existing constraints. We also briefly consider the sensitivity of IceCube to multi-muon events produced by the decays of cosmologically long-lived charged particles with masses $\gtrsim 1$ TeV.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that large-volume neutrino telescopes like IceCube and KM3NeT can search for dark matter through events featuring a pair of energetic, highly non-collimated muon tracks from a common vertex. Since conventional dark matter annihilation/decay is too constrained, the authors propose an excited dark matter state (χ₂) that is extremely long-lived in vacuum but decays rapidly in matter-rich environments via a scalar-field-modified mass spectrum or enhanced kinetic mixing. Two mechanisms are presented, muon energy and opening-angle distributions are calculated, and viable parameter space is shown to yield observable rates consistent with existing constraints.
AI.motivation: To identify a new observable signature of dark matter decay in large-volume neutrino telescopes that avoids the severe constraints on conventional dark matter annihilation/decay, leveraging environment-dependent decay of an excited dark matter state.
AI.method: The authors propose two mechanisms for matter-enhanced decay of an excited dark state χ₂: (1) a long-range scalar field sourced by ordinary matter modifies the dark-sector mass spectrum near Earth, kinematically opening the decay χ₂→χ₁Z'; and (2) the scalar background induces kinetic mixing between a heavy Z' and the photon, enhancing the three-body decay χ₂→χ₁μ⁺μ⁻ in matter-rich environments. They calculate muon energy and opening-angle distributions and assess event rates in IceCube, KM3NeT, and other neutrino telescopes.
AI.result: The calculations show that viable regions of parameter space can yield observable event rates in large-volume neutrino telescopes while remaining consistent with existing constraints. The muon-pair signature has negligible Standard Model backgrounds. The paper also briefly examines IceCube sensitivity to multi-muon events from decays of cosmologically long-lived charged particles with masses ≳1 TeV.
AI.conclusion: Environment-dependent dark matter decay provides a new, testable channel for discovering dark matter via distinctive di-muon events in neutrino telescopes, with two concrete model realizations and favorable prospects for observation.

title: Tree-Level Factorization Obstruction in Monopole Production
summary: We show that the tree-level amplitude for producing a monopole--antimonopole pair from an electrically charged pair cannot be constructed from the minimal one-photon couplings. Gluing the electric and magnetic three-point vertices gives a nonzero photon-pole contribution, but the resulting magnetic final state has the opposite discrete-symmetry eigenvalue from the electric initial state. Local four-point interactions cannot change the pole contribution fixed by the three-point couplings, so they cannot repair this mismatch. For fermions, the obstruction is specific to the minimal three-point coupling: an independent Pauli form factor supplies a spin-singlet three-point amplitude and allows the symmetry selection rule to be satisfied.

AI.tldr: Tree-level monopole-antimonopole pair production from electrically charged pairs cannot be constructed using minimal one-photon couplings alone, because the gluon/vertex gluing produces a final magnetic state with the wrong discrete-symmetry eigenvalue. Local four-point interactions cannot fix this, but an independent Pauli form factor (for fermions) enables a spin-singlet three-point amplitude that satisfies the symmetry selection rule.
AI.motivation: To determine whether minimal one-photon three-point couplings are sufficient to construct a consistent tree-level amplitude for monopole-pair production from electrically charged particles, given that discrete-symmetry selection rules must be respected.
AI.method: Gluing electric and magnetic three-point vertices to construct the four-point amplitude, analyzing the photon-pole contribution, and testing consistency against discrete-symmetry quantum numbers. Examining whether local four-point interactions can alter the pole contribution, and whether an independent Pauli form factor can provide the needed spin-singlet three-point amplitude.
AI.result: The minimal one-photon couplings yield a nonzero photon-pole contribution but produce a magnetic final state with the opposite discrete-symmetry eigenvalue compared to the electric initial state. Local four-point interactions cannot correct this since they cannot change the pole contribution fixed by the three-point vertices. For fermions, an independent Pauli form factor resolves the obstruction by supplying a spin-singlet three-point amplitude that satisfies the selection rule.
AI.conclusion: Minimal one-photon couplings are insufficient for tree-level monopole-pair production from charged pairs due to a discrete-symmetry obstruction. The obstruction is specific to the minimal coupling for fermions and can be circumvented via an independent Pauli form factor.

title: GOOFy-compatible 3HDMs and beyond
summary: Beyond conventional Higgs-family and general CP transformations, one may also consider a broader class of non-standard "GOOFy" transformations, in which the scalar fields and their conjugates are assigned related but inequivalent transformations. Although these transformations are not symmetries of a full Lagrangian in the conventional sense, some nevertheless stabilise the scalar potential. Their impact on the quadratic sector has not yet been systematically classified. We develop a sign-orbit technique to determine the bilinear structures compatible with these transformations. Applied to three-Higgs-doublet models, and formulated so as to extend to larger multi-Higgs sectors, the method shows that a non-vanishing GOOFy-compatible quadratic sector exists only when two independent conditions are met: the underlying group admits a non-trivial sign character, and that character is realised within the tensor product of the scalar representation and its conjugate. As a key consequence, we demonstrate that the renormalisation-group stability of the $r_0 \to -r_0$ manifold in isolation is not a generic feature of multi-Higgs potentials, but rather a direct consequence of special algebraic properties of $SU(2)$. These results provide a classification of the admissible GOOFy quadratic structures and their invariant bilinear subspaces, highlighting the algebraic obstructions to their renormalisation-group stability.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a sign-orbit technique to systematically classify "GOOFy" transformations—non-standard generalized CP transformations where scalar fields and their conjugates transform inequivalently—focusing on their effect on the quadratic (bilinear) sector of multi-Higgs-doublet potentials. Applied to three-Higgs-doublet models, it shows that non-vanishing GOOFy-compatible quadratic sectors exist only under two specific algebraic conditions, and demonstrates that the RG stability of the r0 → −r0 manifold is not generic to multi-Higgs potentials but a special algebraic property of SU(2).
AI.motivation: While unconventional "GOOFy" transformations can stabilize scalar potentials, their impact on the quadratic sector has not been systematically classified, and understanding which bilinear structures are compatible with these transformations is essential for assessing their physical viability and renormalization-group stability in multi-Higgs models.
AI.method: The authors develop a sign-orbit technique to determine the bilinear structures compatible with GOOFy transformations. The method is applied to three-Higgs-doublet models and formulated to extend to larger multi-Higgs sectors, leveraging group-theoretic analysis of sign characters and their realization within tensor products of the scalar representation and its conjugate.
AI.result: A non-vanishing GOOFy-compatible quadratic sector exists only when two independent conditions are met: (1) the underlying group admits a non-trivial sign character, and (2) that character is realized within the tensor product of the scalar representation and its conjugate. The classification reveals all admissible GOOFy quadratic structures and their invariant bilinear subspaces, and shows that RG stability of the r0 → −r0 manifold is not a generic feature but a special consequence of SU(2) algebraic properties.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a complete classification of GOOFy-compatible quadratic structures in multi-Higgs sectors and highlights algebraic obstructions to their renormalization-group stability, demonstrating that stable GOOFy quadratic sectors are highly constrained and that certain RG-stable manifolds arise only from special algebraic features of specific groups like SU(2).

title: Moduli Bounds from Spin-2 Sum Rules
summary: Mirbabayi and Villadoro have provided strong numerical evidence for a universal upper bound on the mass of the lightest scalar field in gravitational Kaluza--Klein (KK) theories. This bound states that the lightest KK graviton, with mass $m_{1}$, must couple to at least one scalar with mass $m_{\rm sc}$ such that $(m_{\rm sc} /m_{1})^2 \leq 4/3$. We give a proof of this bound using the approach of the conformal bootstrap applied to sum rules for massive spin-2 scattering amplitudes. We additionally show that each heavier KK graviton, with mass $m_n$, must couple to at least one scalar with mass $m_{\rm sc}$ such that $(m_{\rm sc} /m_{n})^2 < 36/25$.

AI.tldr: The paper proves a previously conjectured universal upper bound on the mass of the lightest scalar coupled to KK gravitons in gravitational Kaluza-Klein theories using conformal bootstrap techniques applied to massive spin-2 scattering amplitude sum rules. It proves the bound (m_sc/m_1)^2 ≤ 4/3 for the lightest KK graviton and establishes a new bound (m_sc/m_n)^2 < 36/25 for each heavier KK graviton.
AI.motivation: Mirbabayi and Villadoro provided numerical evidence for a universal upper bound on the mass of the lightest scalar field in gravitational Kaluza-Klein (KK) theories. A rigorous analytic proof of this bound was needed, along with extending it to heavier KK gravitons.
AI.method: The authors use the conformal bootstrap approach applied to sum rules for massive spin-2 scattering amplitudes to prove the bound analytically.
AI.result: The proof establishes the bound (m_sc/m_1)^2 ≤ 4/3 for the lightest KK graviton, and proves a new bound (m_sc/m_n)^2 < 36/25 for each heavier KK graviton with mass m_n.
AI.conclusion: The conformal bootstrap provides a rigorous proof of the universal mass bound conjecture for scalar couplings to KK gravitons, confirming the numerical evidence and extending the result to all heavier KK graviton modes.

title: Beyond Borel Windows: A Systematic Optimization Framework for QCD Sum Rules
comment: 13 pages and 5 figures. Presented at the 29th High-Energy Physics International Conference in QCD (QCD26), Montpellier, France
summary: We propose a systematic optimization framework for determining the sum rule window in QCD Laplace sum rules. Instead of relying primarily on fixed convergence percentages and visual plateau selection, the procedure combines an OPE entropy criterion, local mass stationarity, and a correlated analysis of the Laplace parameter $τ$, the continuum threshold $t_c$, and the interpolating-current mixing angle $θ$. The normalized OPE entropy is introduced to quantify the redistribution of the QCD contributions between the perturbative and nonperturbative sectors and to delimit an initial Working Region. This domain is subsequently refined by minimizing the residual variation of the mass estimator and requiring weak sensitivity to the continuum threshold and to the current composition. As an application, we study the lowest fully charmed tetraquark state with quantum numbers $J^{PC}=2^{++}$ using a mixed diquark--antidiquark and meson--meson interpolating current. The optimization selects $θ=17.2^\circ\pm0.4^\circ$, $\sqrt{t_c}=7.08\pm0.08~\mathrm{GeV}$, and $τ=0.410\pm0.010~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$, leading to the mass prediction $M_{c\bar c c\bar c}^{2^{++}}=(6.32\pm0.11)~\mathrm{GeV}$. The predicted state lies in the near-threshold region of the di-$J/ψ$ spectrum and is compatible, within uncertainties, with the lowest resonant component reported by ATLAS and with the enhancement parametrized as $BW_0$ in the recent CMS publication. The proposed framework provides a reproducible way of identifying finite domains of reduced auxiliary-parameter sensitivity and of incorporating the remaining dependence into the final uncertainty.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a systematic optimization framework for determining the sum rule window in QCD Laplace sum rules, combining an OPE entropy criterion, local mass stationarity, and correlated analysis of the Laplace parameter τ, continuum threshold tc, and current mixing angle θ. Applied to the lowest fully charmed tetraquark state with JPC=2++, it predicts a mass of 6.32±0.11 GeV, consistent with the di-J/ψ resonances reported by ATLAS and CMS.
AI.motivation: Traditional QCD sum rule analyses rely on fixed convergence percentages and subjective visual plateau selection to determine the sum rule window. This introduces arbitrariness and lacks reproducibility. The authors aim to replace this with a more principled, systematic optimization framework that objectively identifies stable regions in the auxiliary-parameter space.
AI.method: The framework introduces a normalized OPE entropy that quantifies the redistribution of QCD contributions between perturbative and nonperturbative sectors, delimiting an initial Working Region. This region is refined by minimizing the residual variation of the mass estimator (local mass stationarity) while requiring weak sensitivity to the continuum threshold tc and the current composition parameterized by a mixing angle θ. The method jointly optimizes τ, tc, and θ in a correlated manner.
AI.result: For the fully charmed tetraquark with JPC=2++, the optimization yields θ=17.2°±0.4°, √tc=7.08±0.08 GeV, and τ=0.410±0.010 GeV⁻², producing a mass prediction of M=6.32±0.11 GeV. The predicted state lies near the di-J/ψ threshold and is compatible with the lowest resonant component reported by ATLAS and the BW0 enhancement in the recent CMS publication.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a reproducible, objective way of identifying finite domains of reduced auxiliary-parameter sensitivity in Laplace sum rules, and the residual dependence on parameters is systematically incorporated into the final uncertainty estimate.

title: Adiabatic Deformations of Black Hole Moduli: I. Canonical Slices and Fredholm Solvability
summary: The leading adiabatic response of a static black hole to a slowly evolving asymptotic modulus separates into a geometric problem and a functional-analytic one: the former identifies the tangent direction on the manifold of static solutions actually followed by the black hole, and the latter determines whether the resulting deformation admits a unique solution. We show that both can be characterized by explicit scalar criteria. Differentiating a smooth family of static solutions defines an intrinsic covector on its tangent space. When the family is parameterized by the asymptotic modulus and the static horizon-mass parameter, the kernel of this covector identifies a canonical tangent direction that coincides with the one selected by a slowly varying exterior modulus. Promoting the static family to a slowly evolving instantaneous representative does not solve the exact field equations; the resulting discrepancy defines a lag field governed, after elimination of the metric perturbations, by a single reduced radial operator. A representation convention separates the exact dynamical horizon from that of the instantaneous representative. A local slice then removes the remaining tangential ambiguity and induces a finite-rank perturbation of the reduced operator. The Fredholm index is preserved, and, whenever the finite-rank update is nontrivial, the canonical tangent zero mode is displaced from the kernel of the reduced operator. Under the transversality and Fredholm hypotheses, existence and uniqueness of the completed leading-order adiabatic boundary-value problem reduce to a single scalar matching condition on the resulting kernel generator. The construction depends only on a smooth non-extremal static solution manifold and the Fredholm properties of the reduced operator. A companion paper specializes the framework to the magnetic GHS family.

AI.motivation: To characterize how a static black hole responds adiabatically to a slowly evolving asymptotic modulus. The problem splits into a geometric part (identifying the tangent direction followed on the static solution manifold) and a functional-analytic part (determining whether the resulting deformation admits a unique solution). Both have remained implicit; the authors aim to reduce them to explicit scalar criteria.
AI.method: The method differentiates a smooth family of static solutions to define an intrinsic covector on the tangent space; its kernel selects a canonical tangent direction matching the slowly varying exterior modulus. The static family is promoted to a slowly evolving instantaneous representative, and the discrepancy from exact field equations defines a lag field governed by a single reduced radial operator after eliminating metric perturbations. A representation convention separates exact and instantaneous horizons, and a local slice removes tangential ambiguity, inducing a finite-rank perturbation preserving the Fredholm index. A canonical tangent direction is identified via the kernel of an intrinsic covector. title: Photon-nucleon entanglement in Compton scattering at low and high energies
summary: We study spin-spin entanglement in the final state photon-nucleon system in Compton scattering, both at low energy below the pion threshold and at high energy in perturbative QCD to next-to-leading order. We first establish a no-go theorem showing that, for any spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ target, entanglement cannot be generated in unpolarized Compton scattering if the scattering amplitudes are real. We then consider polarized Compton scattering off the electron, the proton and the neutron. At low energy, we uncover a rich variety of maximally entangled Bell states and their unitary equivalents realized across different regions of the kinematic plane. Interestingly, the proton and neutron targets exhibit distinct patterns of entanglement. In the neutron case, the electric and magnetic polarizabilities dramatically influence the pattern and even the existence of entanglement. This suggests that entanglement can serve as a novel tool for investigating the detailed electromagnetic properties of the nucleons.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates spin-spin entanglement in the final photon-nucleon system from Compton scattering, covering both low-energy (below pion threshold) and high-energy (perturbative QCD at NLO) regimes. A no-go theorem shows entanglement cannot arise in unpolarized Compton scattering off spin-1/2 targets if amplitudes are real. Polarized scattering off electrons, protons, and neutrons reveals rich varieties of maximally entangled Bell states and unitary equivalents, with proton and neutron exhibiting distinct entanglement patterns influenced by electromagnetic polarizabilities.
AI.motivation: To explore whether entanglement in Compton scattering can serve as a novel diagnostic tool for investigating the detailed electromagnetic properties of nucleons, particularly addressing how the proton and neutron differ in their entanglement signatures and how polarizabilities affect entanglement patterns.
AI.method: The authors establish a no-go theorem for entanglement generation in unpolarized Compton scattering with real amplitudes. They then analyze polarized Compton scattering off electron, proton, and neutron targets at low energy (below pion threshold) and at high energy in perturbative QCD to next-to-leading order, examining the entanglement structure of the final-state photon-nucleon system across the kinematic plane.

Proton and neutron targets show distinct entanglement patterns. For the neutron, electric and magnetic polarizabilities dramatically influence both the pattern and existence of entanglement, demonstrating that entanglement measurements could be sensitive to these nucleon properties.
AI.conclusion: Entanglement in Compton scattering can serve as a novel tool for probing the detailed electromagnetic properties of nucleons, with the differential entanglement patterns between proton and neutron potentially providing new insights into their internal structure.

title: Higher-Spin Correlators in dS
summary: We study momentum-space correlators in minimal higher-spin gravity in $\mathrm{dS}_4$ using its holographic vector-model description. Connected $n$-point functions in this model are represented by three-dimensional one-loop integrals and are rational functions of the boundary kinematics. We show that the four-point function displays a nontrivial geometric feature: its physical singularity is governed by a Ptolemy relation for the dual momentum quadrilateral. At five points, the pentagon integral introduces an apparent leading Landau singularity, which we show is spurious and disappears once the Gram constraint is imposed. We derive a representation of the five-point function free of spurious singularities and organized in terms of graph-theoretic building blocks. We then verify the conformal invariance of these correlators and discuss their behavior in the soft, collapsed, and Ptolemy limits. This structure suggests a combinatorial bootstrap for higher-spin correlators at general multiplicity, in which conformal invariance and the physical singularities emerge from the underlying graph combinatorics.

The authors derive a spurious-singularity-free five-point representation built from graph-theoretic blocks, verify conformal invariance, and discuss soft, collapsed, and Ptolemy limits, suggesting a combinatorial bootstrap for higher-spin correlators at general multiplicity.

title: HiggsTools for LHC Run 3 and Beyond
summary: HiggsTools, including the subpackages HiggsPredictions, HiggsBounds, and HiggsSignals, is a toolbox for Beyond-the-SM (BSM) scalar phenomenology at the LHC. It provides BSM model predictions, tests the model against experimental limits from searches for BSM scalars and derives constraints from the measurements of the properties of the discovered Higgs boson. We present a variety of improvements to the HiggsTools framework, preparing it for the results of LHC Run 3 and the HL-LHC. HiggsPredictions now provides additional cross-section predictions for centre-of-mass energies of 13.6 and 14 TeV. Moreover, it now includes cross-section predictions for resonant and non-resonant Higgs-boson pair production. For HiggsBounds, we describe the recasting of searches using multi-top final states, explain their implementation and highlight the impact of the experimental sensitivity of those results. Furthermore, we discuss the implementation of coupling-dependent limits on non-resonant Higgs boson pair production, as well as the improved handling of searches conducted prior to the Higgs boson discovery. For HiggsSignals we describe several improvements for the case of scalars with mass uncertainties.

AI.tldr: The paper presents improvements to HiggsTools, a toolbox for BSM scalar phenomenology at the LHC, preparing it for LHC Run 3 and HL-LHC by adding new cross-section predictions at 13.6 and 14 TeV, resonant and non-resonant Higgs pair production predictions, recasting of multi-top final state searches, coupling-dependent limits on non-resonant Higgs pair production, improved handling of pre-discovery searches, and enhanced treatment of scalars with mass uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To update and improve the HiggsTools framework in preparation for the results of LHC Run 3 and the HL-LHC, ensuring the toolbox remains capable of testing BSM scalar models against new experimental data and constraints.
AI.method: The improvements include: (1) adding cross-section predictions for 13.6 and 14 TeV centre-of-mass energies and for resonant/non-resonant Higgs-boson pair production in HiggsPredictions; (2) recasting multi-top final state searches and implementing coupling-dependent limits on non-resonant Higgs pair production, plus improved handling of pre-discovery searches in HiggsBounds; (3) improving treatment of scalars with mass uncertainties in HiggsSignals.

title: Mass and Force Relations for Extremal E2MD Black Holes
summary: We study static extremal black holes in Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton and two Maxwell fields with independent dilaton couplings $a$ and $b$. When $b=-1/a$ in four dimensions, a time-symmetric initial-value construction allows us to determine the masses and interaction energies of multi-black-hole configurations. On this special locus, the long-range force between any two extremal black holes vanishes. For arbitrary $a$ and $b$, a constant dilaton-shift symmetry, together with homogeneity and the extremality condition, yields a first-order ordinary differential equation that determines the extremal mass as a function of the two electric charges. This equation allows us to analyze the force between non-identical extremal black holes without having to know the explicit black-hole geometry. In all analytically controlled regimes that we examine, the locus $b=-1/a$ separates attractive behavior for $b>-1/a$ from repulsive behavior for $b<-1/a$. We extend the analysis to arbitrary spacetime dimensions, where the corresponding force-cancellation condition is $ab=-2(d-2)/(d-1)$. Finally, we test this sign pattern using the exact $A_2$, $B_2$ and $G_2$ Toda black holes. In the $G_2$ case, a potentially problematic branch is excluded because it contains naked singularities outside the horizon, suggesting an intriguing connection between regularity and the sign of long-range forces.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes static extremal black holes in Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton and two Maxwell fields with independent dilaton couplings a and b. The authors determine masses and interaction energies of multi-black-hole configurations on the special locus b=-1/a in four dimensions where long-range forces vanish. Using a constant dilaton-shift symmetry, homogeneity, and the extremality condition, they derive a first-order ODE for the extremal mass as a function of the two electric charges, enabling force analysis without explicit black-hole geometry. The locus b=-1/a separates attraction (b>-1/a) from repulsion (b<-1/a) in all analytically controlled regimes, and this extends to arbitrary dimensions with the condition ab=-2(d-2)/(d-1). The exact A2, B2, and G2 Toda black holes test this sign pattern, with the G2 case revealing a connection between regularity and force sign.
AI.motivation: To understand the long-range force between non-identical extremal black holes in theories with two Maxwell fields coupled to a dilaton, and to determine the conditions under which these forces vanish, attract, or repel—without requiring explicit black-hole geometries.
AI.method: The authors employ a time-symmetric initial-value construction on the special locus b=-1/a in four dimensions to determine masses and interaction energies. For general a and b, they exploit a constant dilaton-shift symmetry combined with homogeneity and the extremality condition to derive a first-order ODE governing the extremal mass as a function of charges. They then analyze this ODE across analytic regimes and in arbitrary spacetime dimensions, and verify predictions against exact A2, B2, and G2 Toda black-hole solutions.

The exact Toda black-hole tests confirm this sign pattern, except the G2 case has a problematic branch excluded by naked singularities outside the horizon.
AI.conclusion: The force-cancellation condition for multi-extremal-black-hole configurations is established, and the sign of long-range forces correlates with a universal separation locus. The G2 Toda result suggests an intriguing connection between the regularity of solutions (no naked singularities) and the sign of long-range forces, hinting that non-regular branches may be physically excluded.

title: Spinor tunnelling amplitudes from all-order Feynman diagram summation
summary: This work presents a non-perturbative quantum field theoretic computation of spinor tunnelling through a potential barrier. Within position space potential formalism, we identify coupled recursion relations forming a self-consistent integral equation. Our method, enabling both analytical and numerical approaches, transforms into a formalism admitting both numerical framework for arbitrary potentials and analytical exact results for select barriers. For the rectangular barrier, the QFT-derived amplitudes reproduce the relativistic quantum mechanical (RQM) results, thus establishing a foundation for future calculation of beyond-RQM field-theoretic corrections.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a non-perturbative QFT framework for computing spinor tunnelling through potential barriers, using self-consistent integral equations derived from coupled recursion relations in position-space potential formalism. It reproduces RQM results for rectangular barriers and provides a foundation for beyond-RQM corrections.
AI.motivation: To go beyond relativistic quantum mechanics (RQM) in describing tunnelling phenomena by developing a fully field-theoretic, non-perturbative approach that can capture quantum corrections inaccessible to standard quantum mechanical treatments.
AI.method: The authors use a position-space potential formalism in QFT, identifying coupled recursion relations that form a self-consistent integral equation. This allows both analytical solutions (for select barriers) and numerical frameworks (for arbitrary potentials).
AI.result: For the rectangular barrier, the QFT-derived tunnelling amplitudes exactly reproduce the RQM results, validating the framework and establishing it as a reliable baseline for computing beyond-RQM field-theoretic corrections.
AI.conclusion: The non-perturbative QFT formalism provides a solid foundation for future calculations of field-theoretic corrections to tunnelling phenomena, going beyond what RQM can describe.

title: $N$-Photon Amplitudes in EFT from Recursion Relations and Effective Vertices
summary: We present a recursive framework for computing arbitrary tree-level helicity amplitudes in the general effective field theory (EFT) of electromagnetism. We show that photon amplitudes can be constructed using a CSW-like recursion, whose building blocks consist of purely local subamplitudes. For a fixed number of external legs, only a finite number of these contact amplitudes need to be computed, and these admit compact expressions in terms of Hafnians. We further show that the contact amplitudes are encoded in an effective contact Lagrangian, that can be computed systematically from the general EFT Lagrangian using a suitable generating functional. We provide this contact Lagrangian up to $N=14$ photons. We argue that the contact Lagrangian reveals the hidden simplicity of helicity-conserving amplitudes, providing a simple proof of the equivalence between off-shell electromagnetic duality and helicity conservation. We further show how to resum the contact Lagrangian of a helicity-conserving theory to all $N$, and illustrate the procedure for Born-Infeld (BI) electromagnetism. Building on these methods and results, we compute the complete 6-point and 8-point tree-level helicity amplitudes generated by generic EFT operators, and the tree amplitudes up to 10-point in BI electromagnetism.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a CSW-like recursive framework for computing arbitrary tree-level helicity amplitudes in the general EFT of electromagnetism. Photon amplitudes are constructed from purely local subamplitudes (contact amplitudes) that admit compact Hafnian expressions and are encoded in an effective contact Lagrangian, computed up to N=14 photons. The framework reveals the hidden simplicity of helicity-conserving amplitudes, proves the equivalence between off-shell electromagnetic duality and helicity conservation, and demonstrates resummation of the contact Lagrangian to all N for Born-Infeld theory. The methods are applied to compute complete 6- and 8-point tree amplitudes for generic EFT operators and tree amplitudes up to 10-point in BI electromagnetism.
AI.motivation: The goal is to develop a systematic and efficient framework for computing tree-level helicity amplitudes in general EFTs of electromagnetism, which contain infinitely many operators of arbitrarily high dimension. Traditional amplitude computation methods become impractical in this setting, so the authors seek a recursive approach exploiting on-shell recursion (CSW-like) and compact mathematical structures (Hafnians) to organize the computation.
AI.method: The authors introduce a CSW-like (Cachazo-Svrcek-Witten) recursion for photon amplitudes in general EFTs of electromagnetism, where the building blocks are purely local contact subamplitudes. These contact amplitudes admit compact expressions in terms of Hafnians. The contact amplitudes are further encoded in an effective contact Lagrangian, obtained systematically from the general EFT Lagrangian via a suitable generating functional (provided up to N=14 photons). For helicity-conserving theories, the contact Lagrangian is resummed to all orders in N, with the procedure illustrated for Born-Infeld electromagnetism.
AI.result: The framework yields: (1) a CSW-like recursion for photon amplitudes built from local contact subamplitudes; (2) compact Hafnian expressions for contact amplitudes; (3) an effective contact Lagrangian computed up to N=14 photons; (4) a proof of equivalence between off-shell electromagnetic duality and helicity conservation; (5) all-order resummation of the contact Lagrangian for helicity-conserving theories including BI electromagnetism; (6) complete 6-point and 8-point tree-level helicity amplitudes for generic EFT operators; and (7) tree amplitudes up to 10-point in BI electromagnetism.
AI.conclusion: The recursive framework provides a powerful and systematic approach to computing photon amplitudes in general EFTs of electromagnetism, revealing deep structural simplifications for helicity-conserving amplitudes and connecting these to electromagnetic duality. The contact Lagrangian serves as a unifying object that encodes all local contributions and enables all-order resummation for special theories like Born-Infeld.

title: Coherent and Stochastic Axion Dark Matter from Thermal Relaxation
summary: An axion driven toward a thermal minimum need not remain a coherent condensate. We derive the coupled attenuation of the field mean and production of stochastic momentum modes in an expanding plasma. A single momentum dependent optical depth partitions every mode between coherent power and Bose occupation, placing standard misalignment, partial relaxation, and stochastic production in one dynamical relation. Finite spatial and temporal response suppresses high momentum production, so the stochastic relic has lower mean momentum and a shorter free streaming length than an equilibrium population at fixed mass and bath temperature. A weakly coupled realization produces the dark matter abundance, reduces inherited coherent isocurvature, and confines production correlations to scales removed by collisionless propagation. Thermal relaxation therefore determines the composition, momentum distribution, and transported structure of axion dark matter.

AI.tldr: Axion dark matter driven toward a thermal minimum does not necessarily remain a coherent condensate; a single momentum-dependent optical depth governs the partition between coherent power and stochastic mode production, with finite response suppressing high-momentum production and yielding a colder, shorter free-streaming-length relic.
AI.motivation: Previous treatments of axion dark matter assumed coherent misalignment persists even when the axion is pushed toward a thermal minimum. This work aims to unify misalignment, partial relaxation, and stochastic production within a single dynamical framework to correctly determine the relic's composition and momentum distribution.
AI.method: The authors derive the coupled equations for attenuation of the field mean and production of stochastic momentum modes in an expanding plasma, using a single momentum-dependent optical depth that partitions every mode between coherent power and Bose occupation. They account for finite spatial and temporal response to suppress high-momentum production.
AI.result: The stochastic relic has lower mean momentum and shorter free-streaming length than an equilibrium population at fixed mass and bath temperature. A weakly coupled realization can produce the observed dark matter abundance, reduce inherited coherent isocurvature, and confine production correlations to scales erased by collisionless propagation.
AI.conclusion: Thermal relaxation fundamentally determines the composition, momentum distribution, and transported structure of axion dark matter, necessitating a revision of the simple coherent-condensate picture.

title: Adiabatic Deformations of Black Hole Moduli: II. The Magnetic GHS Family
summary: We study the leading adiabatic response of magnetic GHS black holes in massless Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory to a prescribed exterior modulus varying slowly in advanced time. In ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates with the exact areal radius, we derive the time-dependent spherical equations and expand about a slowly evolving instantaneous static GHS representative, keeping its horizon distinct from the exact dynamical marginal horizon. The magnetic GHS family realizes the canonical-slice and Fredholm framework developed in the companion paper. Its integrability yields in closed form the canonical tangent, the finite-rank source profile, a horizon-regular solution of the auxiliary inhomogeneous equation, and a globally regular generator of the sliced-operator kernel. For the leading Robin functional arising in the massless large-radius overlap, we evaluate the Fredholm denominator analytically and prove that it is strictly positive on the charged non-extremal branch. This remains true where the conventional normalization of the kernel generator degenerates, showing that these loci are normalization singularities rather than degeneracies of the kernel mode. Within the controlled large-radius overlap regime, this positivity proves existence and uniqueness of the completed leading-order quasi-static near-zone problem. We then solve the forced radial equation explicitly. The scalar lag is the sum of a universal forced profile and a sliced homogeneous mode whose amplitude is fixed by the exterior matching datum. The mass lag follows algebraically from the radial constraint, and the lapse lag from a single elementary quadrature. The exact marginal horizon is recovered from the lag-corrected solution. The result gives the complete leading quasi-static near-zone response, exact in its radial dependence, for every admissible exterior datum within the specified massless overlap model.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the complete leading-order quasi-static near-zone response of magnetic GHS (Gibbons-Maeda-Sen) black holes in massless Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory to a slowly varying exterior modulus, using the canonical-slice and Fredholm framework. The authors derive explicit closed-form solutions for the canonical tangent, kernel generator, Fredholm denominator, and all response lags (scalar, mass, and lapse), proving existence and uniqueness via strict positivity of the Fredholm denominator.
AI.motivation: To compute the adiabatic response of magnetic GHS black holes to slowly varying exterior perturbations, and to validate the general canonical-slice/Fredholm framework from the companion paper on an exactly integrable example, thereby clarifying whether apparent kernel degeneracies are physical or mere normalization singularities.
AI.method: Work in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates with exact areal radius; expand time-dependent spherical equations about a slowly evolving instantaneous static GHS representative; apply the canonical-slice and Fredholm framework; exploit integrability of the magnetic GHS family to compute in closed form the canonical tangent, finite-rank source profile, horizon-regular solution of the auxiliary inhomogeneous equation, and a globally regular kernel generator; evaluate the Robin functional and Fredholm denominator analytically; solve the forced radial equation explicitly for scalar, mass, and lapse lags; recover the exact marginal horizon from the lag-corrected solution.
AI.result: The Fredholm denominator is proven strictly positive on the charged non-extremal branch, including where the conventional kernel-generator normalization degenerates—showing those loci are normalization singularities, not true degeneracies. This positivity establishes existence and uniqueness of the completed leading-order quasi-static near-zone problem in the controlled large-radius overlap regime. The scalar lag decomposes into a universal forced profile plus a sliced homogeneous mode fixed by the exterior datum; the mass lag follows algebraically, the lapse lag from a single quadrature, and the exact marginal horizon is recovered from the lag-corrected solution, giving the complete quasi-static response exact in radial dependence.
AI.conclusion: The magnetic GHS family provides a fully solvable realization of the canonical-slice/Fredholm framework, yielding explicit closed-form leading-order quasi-static near-zone response for all admissible exterior data. The strict positivity of the Fredholm denominator resolves the apparent kernel-degeneracy question in favor of normalization singularities, and the explicit solutions complete the quasi-static near-zone problem within the massless overlap model.

title: Revisiting the $Λ_c^+ \to nπ^+η$ decay in light of the BESIII measurement
summary: Motivated by the latest BESIII measurements on $Λ_c^+\to nπ^+η$, we perform a systematic theoretical study of this decay. We take into account contributions from the $N(1535)$ state dynamically generated by $S$-wave pseudoscalar meson-octet baryon interactions, the $a_0(980)$ resonance originating from the $S$-wave pseudoscalar meson-pseudoscalar meson interactions, together with the intermediate states $N(1440)$ and $a_2(1320)$. Our results indicate that $a_0(980)$ provides a significant contribution to this process. The inclusion of $a_2(1320)$ hardly improves the fitting quality, while the nucleon resonances play a crucial role in describing the experimental behavior of the $π^+η$ invariant mass spectrum in both low and high energy regions. Restricted by insufficient experimental statistics and a coarse bin size of 33 MeV, the precise contribution fraction of $a_0(980)$ cannot be reliably extracted. We propose future higher-precision and higher-statistics experimental measurements of $Λ_c^+\to nπ^+η$, which can help reveal the intrinsic nature of $a_0(980)$ and quantify the roles of different excited nucleon states in this decay.

AI.tldr: A systematic theoretical study of the decay Λ_c^+ → nπ^+η, motivated by BESIII measurements, examining contributions from dynamically generated N(1535), a0(980), N(1440), and a2(1320) resonances. a0(980) contributes significantly, nucleon resonances are crucial for describing the π^+η invariant mass spectrum, but the a0(980) contribution fraction cannot be reliably extracted due to limited statistics.
AI.motivation: To understand the decay Λ_c^+ → nπ^+η in light of new BESIII measurements, particularly to probe the intrinsic nature of the a0(980) resonance and clarify the roles of various intermediate states, especially nucleon resonances and dynamically generated states.
AI.method: A theoretical analysis incorporating contributions from the N(1535) state dynamically generated by S-wave pseudoscalar meson-octet baryon interactions, the a0(980) resonance from S-wave pseudoscalar meson-pseudoscalar meson interactions, and intermediate states N(1440) and a2(1320), fitted to BESIII data.
AI.result: a0(980) provides a significant contribution; including a2(1320) hardly improves fit quality; nucleon resonances are crucial for describing the π^+η invariant mass spectrum in both low and high energy regions; precise extraction of the a0(980) contribution fraction is hindered by insufficient statistics and a 33 MeV bin size.
AI.conclusion: Future higher-precision and higher-statistics measurements of Λ_c^+ → nπ^+η are needed to reveal the intrinsic nature of a0(980) and quantify the roles of different excited nucleon states in this decay.

title: Interacting Galilean and Finite-Energy Carroll Fermions
summary: We present a unified derivation of the Galilean and Carrollian limits of the massive Dirac action based on a similarity transformation depending on the mass and the speed of light. The two choices of Dirac conjugation, combined with different mass scalings, generate distinct families of limiting actions. This construction recovers known Galilei and Carroll fermion models and yields new systems, one in each regime. We classify a sufficient set of boost-compatible local (self-)interactions, which includes Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL). The new Galilean free action possesses a local fermionic gauge symmetry that eliminates its local field content. A selected quartic interaction, preserving the Bargmann boost, explicitly breaks the original fermionic gauge symmetry so that the argument that eliminates the field content no longer applies. The NJL limit interaction merely deforms the realization of that gauge symmetry. We show that the energy parameter in several Carroll actions can be eliminated by a time-dependent phase redefinition; conversely, in the new Carrollian extension the energy cannot be removed.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a unified formalism for deriving Galilean and Carrollian limits of the massive Dirac action via a mass- and speed-of-light-dependent similarity transformation. The construction yields known fermion models plus new ones, classifies boost-compatible self-interactions including NJL, and analyzes gauge symmetries and energy parameters in the resulting theories.
AI.motivation: To provide a systematic, unified framework for obtaining non-relativistic (Galilean) and ultra-relativistic (Carrollian) limits of massive fermionic theories, recovering existing models while discovering new ones with novel symmetry properties.
AI.method: The authors use a similarity transformation depending on mass and speed of light to derive limiting actions. They explore two choices of Dirac conjugation combined with different mass scalings, classify boost-compatible local self-interactions (including NJL), and analyze gauge symmetries and energy parameter elimination via time-dependent phase redefinitions.
AI.result: Known Galilei and Carroll fermion models are recovered, and new systems are found in each regime. The new Galilean free action has a local fermionic gauge symmetry that removes local field content; a quartic interaction explicitly breaks this symmetry, while the NJL limit deforms its realization. Energy can be eliminated in several Carroll actions via phase redefinitions but not in the new Carrollian extension.
AI.conclusion: The unified derivation provides a complete classification of limiting Dirac fermion actions in both non-relativistic and ultra-relativistic regimes, revealing novel models and clarifying the fate of gauge symmetries and energy parameters under these limits.

title: Net electron spin rotation in a plane-wave pulse: Holonomy set by the anomalous magnetic moment
comment: 24 pages, 4 figures, 10 tables. Single-file preprint: the article (Secs. I-VIII) followed by its Supplemental Material as an appendix (Secs. S1-S7). Submitted to Physical Review D. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21758393
summary: We compute the spin rotation that survives after a relativistic electron has crossed a plane-wave laser pulse of finite duration. In the interaction picture built on the exact $g=2$ evolution, the Thomas-Bargmann-Michel-Telegdi equation becomes parallel transport by a connection with constant coefficients on the polarization plane, and the pulse enters only through the closed curve that the transverse vector potential traces there. The net rotation is the holonomy of that connection: an angle $-\frac{1}{2}a_e^2\mathcal{A}$ about the propagation direction, with $a_e=(g-2)/2$ the anomaly and $\mathcal{A}$ twice the signed area enclosed by the curve. That area is the spin angular momentum the pulse carries per unit area, so the rotation measures the helicity of the light. Reduction of the residual dynamics to a rotation coupled through the anomaly alone is an exact result of the 1960s [Ternov, Bagrov, and Klimenko, Sov. Phys. J. 11, 29 (1968); Bagrov and Gitman, The Dirac Equation and its Solutions (De Gruyter, Berlin, 2014), Sec. 5.3], which yields two closed-form cases; the area law is the general second order that those two cases bound. The same area governs the orientation memory of a neutral magnetic dipole [Oblak and Seraj, Phys. Rev. D 109, 044037 (2024)] with a coupling of order unity. For a charged electron on a Volkov orbit the coupling $g/2$ cancels identically, which suppresses the rotation by $1.3\times10^{-6}$ and leaves a channel with no $g$-independent part. We verify the cancellation at $g=2$ over 180 pulse configurations and the area law over 89 more. Finite focusing restores that part at second order in $1/kw_0$, and it exceeds the anomalous signal unless $w_0\gtrsim16λ$ at $γ=10$, or $270λ$ at $γ=1$.

AI.tldr: The paper computes the spin rotation of a relativistic electron after traversing a finite-duration plane-wave laser pulse, showing the net rotation is a holonomy given by −1/2 a_e² A, where a_e is the electron's magnetic anomaly and A is twice the signed area traced by the transverse vector potential — a quantity equal to the pulse's spin angular momentum per unit area, thus measuring light helicity. The area law generalizes two closed-form cases from 1960s results, and the same area governs magnetic dipole orientation memory. For a charged electron on a Volkov orbit, the g/2 coupling cancels identically, suppressing rotation by ~1.3×10⁻⁶; finite focusing restores this channel at second order in 1/kw₀, exceeding the anomalous signal unless tight focusing conditions are met.
AI.motivation: To derive a general, closed-form expression for the net spin rotation of a relativistic electron interacting with a finite plane-wave laser pulse, extending known two limiting cases (from Ternov–Bagrov–Klimenko) to an arbitrary pulse shape via a geometric (holonomy/area) law, and to identify the pulse parameters under which the anomalous (g−2) contribution dominates over the leading coupling term.
AI.method: The authors work in an interaction picture built on the exact g=2 evolution, where the Thomas–Bargmann–Michel–Telegdi (T-BMT) equation reduces to parallel transport by a connection with constant coefficients on the polarization plane. The pulse enters only through the closed curve the transverse vector potential traces, and the net rotation is identified as the holonomy of this connection. The general result is verified numerically against exact Volkov solutions: over 180 pulse configurations at g=2 (cancellation check) and over 89 configurations (area law check). Finite-focusing corrections are treated perturbatively to second order in 1/kw₀.
AI.result: The net spin rotation angle is −1/2 a_e² A, with A being twice the signed area enclosed by the vector-potential curve (equal to the light's spin angular momentum per unit area). This area law reproduces the two closed-form cases of the 1960s results as special cases and unifies them at second order. For a charged electron on a Volkov orbit, the g/2 coupling cancels identically regardless of pulse shape, suppressing the rotation by 1.3×10⁻⁶ and leaving a channel with no g-independent part. Numerical verification confirms the cancellation at g=2 and the area law. Finite focusing restores the leading g-independent rotation at second order in 1/kw₀, and this exceeds the anomalous signal unless w₀ ≳ 16λ at γ=10 or 270λ at γ=1.
AI.conclusion: The spin rotation of an electron crossing a finite plane-wave pulse is a purely geometric quantity — the holonomy of a constant-coefficient connection on the polarization plane — governed by the signed area of the vector-potential curve, i.e., the pulse helicity. This gives a clean, general two-order area law that encompasses earlier closed-form results. For Volkov electrons the leading coupling contribution cancels exactly (a special consequence of the g/2 factor), isolating the anomalously suppressed rotation, but realistic transverse focusing reinstates a larger non-anomalous rotation for wide parameter ranges, with the anomalous signal only dominating under sufficiently tight focusing conditions.

title: Exact Lattice Identities and Continuum-Limit Dyson--Schwinger Equations for Yang-Mills Theory
summary: Starting from SU(N) on the lattice, we give a rigorous derivation of the Dyson--Schwinger equations in the continuum limit. We formulate the Dyson--Schwinger identities for the lattice Yang--Mills theory directly in terms of the link variables $U_μ(m)\in SU(N)$, exploiting the invariance of the Haar measure under left group translations. This provides an exact lattice derivation of the corresponding master equation for the Wilson action, expressed through left-invariant Lie derivatives acting on individual links. Because the construction is carried out directly on the compact gauge group, it avoids the ambiguities associated with introducing Lie-algebra valued gauge potentials as primary integration variables at finite lattice spacing. For practical applications, in a second part we then break down the gauge degree of freedom by choosing Feynman gauge. We analyze the continuum-limit form of the resulting lattice identities and derive equations for the one- and two-point connected functions. Under a further simplifying reduction, these equations close to a tractable scalar system. Our results establish a direct bridge between exact lattice identities and the functional equations commonly used in continuum nonperturbative studies of Yang--Mills theory.

AI.tldr: The paper rigorously derives Dyson-Schwinger equations for lattice Yang-Mills theory directly using SU(N) link variables, exploiting left-invariant Haar measure properties, then formulates them in Feynman gauge and analyzes their continuum limit to connect lattice identities with continuum functional equations.
AI.motivation: To provide an exact lattice derivation of Dyson-Schwinger identities that avoids ambiguities from introducing Lie-algebra-valued gauge potentials as primary integration variables at finite lattice spacing, and to establish a rigorous bridge between exact lattice identities and continuum functional equations used in nonperturbative Yang-Mills studies.
AI.method: The derivation is performed directly on compact SU(N) gauge group using link variables U_μ(m), exploiting left-invariant Haar measure properties. Left-invariant Lie derivatives acting on individual links formulate the master equation for the Wilson action. The gauge freedom is then fixed via Feynman gauge, and the continuum-limit form of lattice identities is analyzed to derive equations for one- and two-point connected functions, with a further reduction to a tractable scalar system.
AI.result: Exact lattice Dyson-Schwinger identities expressed through left-invariant Lie derivatives on links, their Feynman-gauge fixed continuum-limit forms, and equations for one- and two-point connected functions that close to a tractable scalar system under simplifying assumptions.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a direct and rigorous bridge between exact lattice Dyson-Schwinger identities and the functional equations commonly used in continuum nonperturbative Yang-Mills theory, resolving ambiguities present in prior formulations.

title: Machine Learning is Good for Physics - and Vice Versa
summary: Scientific AI is rapidly transforming fundamental physics research and challenging defining aspects of the fundamental physics methodology. We discuss opportunities and dangers of this transformation and find exciting benefits from a close interaction between AI and fundamental physics, provided that we remain aware of the scientific methodologies of the respective fields. For fundamental physics, we discuss two such aspects: statistical validation and a generalizing theory description, both with the goal of discovering new physics in vast datasets.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses how AI is transforming fundamental physics research, examining both the opportunities and dangers of this transformation, and argues that while AI offers exciting benefits for physics, researchers must remain mindful of the distinct scientific methodologies of both fields—particularly statistical validation and generalizing theory description—when using AI to discover new physics in vast datasets.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the rapid transformation of fundamental physics research by AI, which challenges defining aspects of physics methodology. The authors aim to analyze both the opportunities and dangers of this shift and to clarify how physics and AI can beneficially interact while respecting the scientific standards of each field.
AI.method: The paper provides a conceptual/discussion-based analysis focused on two key aspects of fundamental physics methodology—statistical validation and generalizing theory description—as they intersect with AI-based approaches to discovering new physics in large datasets.
AI.result: The paper finds that close interaction between AI and fundamental physics offers exciting benefits, provided practitioners remain aware of the distinct scientific methodologies of both fields.
AI.conclusion: The transformation of physics by AI presents substantive opportunities but also carries dangers; the key to productive collaboration lies in maintaining methodological awareness—specifically of statistical validation and generalizing theory description—in both AI and fundamental physics research.

title: Surviving correlations across a horizon: reflected entropy for bosonic fields in non-inertial frames and black hole spacetimes
summary: We study the reflected entropy and the Markov gap for modes of a free bosonic field shared by inertial observers (Alice, Charlie) and a uniformly accelerated one (Bob), for a bipartite Bell state and the tripartite Werner (W) and Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states. The bosonic Bogoliubov transformation spans an infinite-dimensional Fock space with an unbounded squeezing parameter unlike the fermionic case. By identifying a conserved charge, we block-diagonalize the reduced density matrices into exact two-dimensional sectors, yielding closed or semi-analytic forms for all three states. Although bosonic entanglement is known to vanish asymptotically, the Alice--Bob reflected entropy instead saturates at a nonzero saturation floor, retaining the surviving classical correlation, and converges to the value Alice shares with Bob's causally disconnected partner. Crucially, only the inter-wedge reflected entropy diverges, linearly in the squeezing parameter---the sharp distinction from the fermionic case, where it stays bounded---while the Markov gaps saturate. The construction transfers verbatim to a Schwarzschild black hole, where the saturation values become mass-independent constants.

AI.tldr: The paper studies reflected entropy and Markov gap for free bosonic field modes shared by inertial observers (Alice, Charlie) and a uniformly accelerated observer (Bob) for Bell, Werner, and GHZ states. Using a conserved charge to block-diagonalize reduced density matrices into exact two-dimensional sectors, they obtain closed or semi-analytic forms. While bosonic entanglement vanishes asymptotically, Alice–Bob reflected entropy saturates at a nonzero floor retaining classical correlations, and only the inter-wedge reflected entropy diverges linearly in the squeezing parameter (unlike fermions where it stays bounded). The construction transfers to Schwarzschild black holes where saturation values become mass-independent constants.
AI.motivation: To understand how reflected entropy and Markov gaps behave for bosonic fields in relativistic settings (Unruh effect), particularly to characterize the classical vs. quantum correlations surviving the asymptotic vanishing of bosonic entanglement, and to contrast with the fermionic case where the Fock space is finite-dimensional.
AI.method: The bosonic Bogoliubov transformation spans an infinite-dimensional Fock space with unbounded squeezing parameter. A conserved charge is identified to block-diagonalize the reduced density matrices into exact two-dimensional sectors, enabling closed or semi-analytic expressions for reflected entropy and Markov gaps for bipartite Bell, tripartite W, and GHZ states.
AI.result: Alice–Bob reflected entropy saturates at a nonzero floor (retaining surviving classical correlation), converging to the value Alice shares with Bob's causally disconnected partner. title: Descoped and Upscoped FCC-ee Running Scenarios in the SMEFT
summary: We present projections for the sensitivity to new physics of descoped and upscoped FCC-ee scenarios in the framework of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). We also analyse the possibility of a staged top-quark run, where the top-quark run is partially restored in case funding becomes available only at a later stage. Motivated by the trade-off between beam power and operational costs, we also consider two upscoped scenarios, either through a uniform increase in luminosity across all energy runs, or through a luminosity enhancement targeting exclusively the top-quark run. We explore the sensitivity and limitations of each scenario and highlight in particular the complementarity between the FCC-ee projections and the (HL)-LHC measurements. By comparing the physics impact of the different running scenarios with the FCC-ee baseline, we show explicitly the importance of the top-quark run, indicating that a substantial fraction of the FCC-ee physics potential depends on it.

title: From chiral to conformal anomalies: a double copy perspective for CFT correlators
summary: We uncover a double-copy relation between chiral and conformal anomalies in four-dimensional conformal field theory. title: Information-Theoretic Black Hole Entropy I: Beyond the Area Law
summary: Although the Bekenstein-Hawking area law is consistent with the first and second laws of black hole thermodynamics, it appears to be in conflict with the third law, which in the Nernst formulation states that the entropy should either vanish or approach a universal constant in the zero-temperature limit. We argue that this tension reflects a limitation of the semiclassical area law rather than a fundamental feature of black hole thermodynamics. On this basis, we obtain an entropy formula that is consistent with the third law, and approaches Bekenstein-Hawking entropy in the high-temperature limit. The resulting entropy admits a simple microscopic interpretation, and it can be written as the Kullback-Leibler divergence between a mass-biased Bernoulli distribution and the uniform distribution on N microscopic bits. From this perspective, the thermodynamic black hole entropy admits an information-theoretic representation as an entropy deficit, namely as the relative entropy between the black hole ensemble and a maximally mixed reference ensemble. The Bekenstein-Hawking area law then emerges as the leading term in an $1/N$ expansion, while a universal mass scale $M_0=\sqrt{N}\,M_P$, interpreted as an absolute upper bound on the black hole mass, controls the bias of the underlying microscopic ensemble. The subleading terms represent finite-information corrections to the classical area law.

title: Impact of dimension-8 SMEFT operators on baryogenesis via sphaleron decoupling
summary: We investigate whether a baryogenesis mechanism known as sphalerogenesis can account for the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe within the Standard Model effective field theory. We introduce seven $CP$-violating dimension-8 operators constructed from the Higgs doublet and the $SU(2)_L$ gauge fields and show that five of them can individually account for the observed baryon asymmetry with satisfying experimental constraints from colliders or electron electric dipole moment measurements. We further study their impact in the presence of a $CP$-violating dimension-6 operator. We find that the dimension-8 contributions can be comparable to the dimension-6 contribution when the dimension-8 operators are generated at one loop, demonstrating that loop-order counting can be as important as canonical mass-dimension counting in sphalerogenesis.

title: Information--Theoretic Black Hole Entropy II: Infrared Gravity and Charged/Rotating Extensions
summary: We investigate gravitational and Kerr-Newman extensions of an information-theoretic black-hole entropy that satisfies the Nernst formulation of the third law of thermodynamics. This construction preserves the connection with the horizon area and the semiclassical limit, while distinguishing geometrical extremality from the universal statistical-freezing endpoint, which is independent of angular momentum and charge.

title: Infrared singularities and the collinear limits of multi-leg scattering amplitudes
comment: 4 pages, 2 figures. Contribution to the 2026 QCD session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: Scattering amplitudes admit a factorised structure in special kinematic limits, such as the soft and collinear limits. We show through four loops that the requirements on the structure of the massless soft anomalous dimension that are imposed by strict collinear factorisation in all two-particle collinear limits are enough to guarantee factorisation also in any multi-particle collinear limit. title: Emergent gravitational action from non-local $T\bar T$-like deformations
summary: We study the gravitational effective action induced, at first order in the deformation parameter, by non-local $T\bar T$-like deformations of quantum field theories. Using a heat-kernel formulation, we extract the local geometric terms generated by stress-tensor two-point functions, and apply the construction to free fermions, massive Maxwell theory, and second-order Yang-Mills theory. While the resulting coefficients are generally model dependent, conformal field theories contain a universal sector fixed by the central charge $C_T$. After regularization and renormalization, this sector yields finite, scheme-independent contributions organized into a finite set of curvature invariants. We further analyze trace-trace deformations, for which the relevant contact terms are determined by the Weyl anomaly, and derive the corresponding finite gravitational action for a general class of minimal non-local kernels. These results provide a quantum effective-action realization of induced gravity in which universal conformal data determine calculable contributions to the emergent geometric response.

title: Three-Loop Five-Point CK-Dual Amplitudes and UV Structure in N=4 SYM and N=8 SUGRA
summary: We construct the complete full-color three-loop five-point integrand of N=4 super-Yang--Mills theory in a representation that manifestly satisfies color--kinematics duality. Extending the external-state dependence to D dimensions is subtle. We consider a candidate replacement of the four-dimensional prefactors by expressions built from D-dimensional tree amplitudes. title: Scalar Hair at the String-Black-Hole Correspondence
summary: We study static, spherically symmetric axion--dilaton solutions of the tree-level four-dimensional string effective action. Using the sigma-model structure of the scalar sector, we show that the full family of static, spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat solutions is obtained as the $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ orbit of the pure-dilaton FJNW solution, and we characterize the associated axion--dilaton charge space. We then analyze the perturbative regime of these solutions by comparing the onset of $α'$ curvature corrections with that of string-loop corrections. Finally, we apply the string--black-hole correspondence criterion to the FJNW family by evaluating the local $α'$ curvature diagnostic at the physical size $R_{\rm typ}$ of a highly excited string state. With the normalization fixed on the Schwarzschild branch, Schwarzschild saturates the nominal $α'$ threshold at the correspondence surface, whereas every scalar-haired FJNW branch lies above it. More generally, independently of the common overall normalization within the matching prescription, every nonzero-hair branch has a larger curvature diagnostic at the correspondence surface than Schwarzschild. Away from the correspondence point, scalar-haired exteriors may remain under $α'$ control at sufficiently weak local self-gravity and may provide perturbatively controlled long-distance fields of highly excited string states whenever the local string coupling also remains weak.

title: Partition Functions of Hermitian and PT-Symmetric Oscillators from Integrable Models

title: Integrable models of inflation beyond slow-roll
summary: We propose a novel analytic approach to the study of multi-component FLRW cosmologies and their perturbations. The dynamics is triggered by a single scalar field with a scalar potential codifying the energy density and pressure of the multi-component fluid. This description unifies standard Big Bang cosmologies, models of inflation and dark energy under a unique framework. The key to integrability is to express the scalar potential in terms of the Hubble function $H(φ)$ that plays the role of a fake superpotential, turning the dynamics into a first order problem, that may be analytically solved in a suitable time coordinate. In this framework, we propose integrable inflationary models with similar properties to the ones analysed in the literature and compatible with observations. Finally, we study scalar and tensor cosmological perturbations in each model by integrating Mukhanov-Sasaki equations via numerical and (semi-)analytic techniques. This allow us to compute the power spectrum, the spectral indices and the tensor-to-scalar ratio beyond the slow-roll approximation and compare our general results {against} the currently available observations and the theoretical predictions based on the slow-roll approximation.
